identification: Cherubino da Spoleto OFM (1414-1484), Sermones quadragesimales: the sermon on God's clemency toward the returning sinner
note: Eleven consecutive line-ends match the Venice 1502 edition (Arrivabene), p. 346 in the Google Books copy. Leaf is therefore 15th-century, not 11th.

dimensions: Front pastedown: 485 x 250; back pastedown: 485 x 250 – 255 mm
catalogue_title: Unidentified commentary on the Book of Genesis
identification: Nicholas of Lyra, Tractatus de differentia nostrae translationis ab hebraica littera (1333), Genesis 2:18-6:16 and 16:13-28:18
note: About forty consecutive lines verbatim against the Rouen 1507 edition (Sainte-Geneviève copy). Not the Postilla litteralis.

identification: Johannes Balbus, Catholicon (1286), letter C: Cain-Catinus and Cibus-Cilicia, two non-consecutive leaves
note: About 25 entries across four sides match the Strasbourg Rusch print (c. 1475-77) in order and wording; the text cites itself ('in iiii. parte dixi').

identification: Nicholas of Lyra, Postilla litteralis super Epistolam ad Hebraeos, cap. 5 (Heb 5:1-9)
note: Fifteen anchor points in edition order against the Venice 1603 Glossa ordinaria with Lyra, vol. 6; genre is a biblical postill, not a homily.

identification: Richard of Middleton OFM, Quaestio disputata de gradu formarum (c. 1286): the 'leprosus generat leprosum' proof and the three impossibilia
note: Six passages verbatim against the excerpts Hocedez printed from Paris, Arsenal 516 (1925). Leaf order in the catalogue is reversed. Page spans in Zavalloni's 1951 edition still to add.

institution: Leuven, Archief van de Abdij van Park
catalogue_title: Gloss on unidentified canon law text
identification: Guido de Baysio (Archidiaconus), Rosarium super Decreto, on C. 10 q. 1 c. 13-14 and q. 2 pr.
note: Six consecutive lines verbatim against the incunable Rosarium (1473, 1480, 1495). Not the Glossa ordinaria.

catalogue_title: Commentarium super IV librum Sententiarum (unidentified), dd. 15
identification: Anonymous abbreviatio of Lombard IV: mnemonic verses = pseudo-Bonaventure Sententiae Sententiarum; chapter summaries = the summa distinctionis later built into Jan Hus's Super IV Sententiarum
note: Both layers matched to printed parallels (Peltier 1866; Flajšhans 1906); French, late 14th century, so an earlier witness of Hus's source. Compiler anonymous.

catalogue_title: Unidentified theological treatise, containing a fragment of Summa Theologiae
identification: A both-laws compendium reworking Aquinas, Summa theologiae IIa-IIae q. 10 a. 11-12 and q. 11 a. 1, with Roman-law and Decretum citations added
note: Twelve consecutive lines of q. 10 a. 11 nearly verbatim (Corpus Thomisticum); the compiling work is unprinted and unidentified.

identification: An alphabetical tabula of auctoritates (Modestia to Mors) with chapter and pericope-letter references; not a lexicon
note: Every quotation traced to its source (Ambrose, Cicero, Aristotle, Augustine, Jerome, Seneca, Gregory). Compilation unidentified; Jean de Fayt's Tabulae are the lead candidate.

identification: A Franciscan commentary on Sentences Book I, one question near d. 20 (innascibilitas as the ratio of generation and primacy)
note: Position fixed by internal cross-references; quotes William of Auvergne's 'unmarked sheep'. Unedited; Francis of Meyronnes and the Walter of Bruges circle are the leads.

identification: A didactic poem in unrhymed hexameters on the sacraments (eucharist, confirmation, chrism, viaticum, Easter communion), divided into 'dietae', after 1215
note: About forty distinctive phrases return nothing in Google Books, archive.org or Corpus Corporum; unprinted. Next step is Walther's Initia carminum by dieta incipit.

identification: Hippocrates, De regimine acutorum (Articella version), end of Book II, with Galen's commentary in the Arabic-Latin translation
note: Running title REG / ACUT; lemma and commentary match the Venice 1491 Articella line by line (14-row table). The 'gloss' is Galen's commentary itself.

identification: Bernardus Compostellanus iunior, Lectura in primum librum Decretalium, on X 1.6.23 Bonae memoriae and 1.6.24 Querelam (De electione)
note: Column A lines 2-66 and column B 1-31 near verbatim against the Paris 1516 Lectura aurea, fol. 55v-56v. Canon law; the Digest citations are the canonist's allegations.

identification: Robert Holcot OP, Super Sapientiam Salomonis, end of lectio II and start of lectio III (Wis 1:1-2)
note: Fifteen anchor points against the Hagenau 1494 edition's page images, incl. the dubium on the theological virtues and the rhymed divisio Rectitudo / Gratitudo / Sollicitudo / Altitudo. Leaf is wrapped sideways round the book.

identification: Contains Guillelmus Durantis, Speculum iudiciale II.3 De appellationibus § Nunc breviter nn. 13-14 verbatim; the rest of the leaf, on the same subject, is not in the printed Speculum
note: Eleven consecutive lines match the Lyon 1578 print; the auditor's name reads 'magistro .h.' where the print has 'Gulielmo Durandi'. Either an earlier recension or the curial source Durantis condensed.

identification: A medical florilegium on sleep and excessive sleep ('In libro X, Auctor:' excerpts from Avicenna, Hippocrates, Aristotle, Johannitius, Constantine), in the manner of Arnoldus Saxo's Practica de causis morborum
note: Excerpts verified verbatim against the Canon and the Aphorisms; the compilation matches Draelants's description of Arnoldus's Practica, known from one Oxford manuscript, which is not online. Central bifolium of its quire.

institution: Leuven, KU Leuven Bibliotheken Bijzondere Collecties
identification: Two texts: (1) an anonymous scholastic commentary on Hippocrates, Aphorisms VII.53-59; (2) a chapter table of a Latin Galen collection (De ingenio sanitatis IV-XIV, De interioribus)
note: Aphorism lemmata verified against the 1519 Articella; the commentary's own prose ('Quia in afforismo iam habito determinavit ypocrates') matches nothing printed. Taddeo Alderotti 1527 to read by eye.

identification: A Thomist-school quaestio commentary on Aristotle, Metaphysics VII cc. 4-5 (quod quid erat esse and definition), quoting Aquinas's Sententia libri Metaphysicae VII lect. 4 nearly verbatim
note: Question apparatus (notabilia, conclusiones, corollaria) absent from Aquinas; Johannes Versor's printed Quaestiones or a Cologne/Louvain course are the candidates, none with usable OCR.

identification: An arts-faculty question commentary on Aristotle's De longitudine et brevitate vitae and De morte et vita (natural heat and radical moisture; whether the hot and moist live longer than the temperate)
note: Central bifolium of its quire, four sides continuous. Buridan ruled out on wording; John of Jandun's Quaestiones super Parvis naturalibus is the lead, no searchable text. Six anchor phrases return nothing.

institution: Leuven, Archief van de Abdij van Park
catalogue_title: Legendary: unidentified life of St Gregory the Illuminator, ch. 3-7
identification: A Latin life of Gregory the Illuminator abridged from the Greek recension of Agathangelos (name forms Asichina, Terdatius, Valarsapath), divided into titled sections of numbered chapters; Rhipsime martyrdom and the baptism in the Euphrates
note: Not matched to BHL 3664 (Acta Sanctorum Sept. VIII), whose ending differs; no readable copy of the edition was reachable. Same manuscript as F-hcpv, outer bifolium. Recto/verso labels for two images are swapped in the record.

institution: Leuven, Archief van de Abdij van Park
catalogue_title: Legendary: unidentified legend on St Gregory the Illuminator, ch. 1-5
identification: The final section of the same Latin life as F-0kql: Trdat and Gregory in Rome with Constantine and Silvester, Aristakes at Nicaea, Gregory's death; the text ends on fol. 2r
note: Innermost bifolium of its quire, holding the end of the work. Same hand and layout as F-0kql; roughly one to three leaves lost between them.

catalogue_title: Unidentified commentary on a religious text
identification: A scholastic lemma-and-exposition commentary in two columns with underlined lemmata, cross-references by chapter and to Paul; the written side faces outward and is worn to near-illegibility
note: Channel separation recovered isolated words only; the better-preserved inner face is under paper pastedowns. No search was possible. Needs UV or raking-light imaging.
